newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon 1996 wheat crop about 21,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon 1996 wheat crop about 21,000 tonnes.

text.p: Lebanon produced some 21,000 tonnes of wheat in 1996, about the same as a year earlier, the office of cereals and sugar beet said on Tuesday.

"We bought some 16,000 tonnes of wheat from farmers, so I estimate that the whole crop does not exceed 21,000 tonnes as they sell a few thousand tonnes to the private sector or keep some for themselves," a cereals office official told Reuters.
The cereals office, which is part of the economy ministry, reported that Lebanon produced 20,000 tonnes of wheat in 1995. This compared with 21,000 tonnes in 1994 and some 25,000 tonnes in 1993.
Lebanon has annual wheat needs of 400,000 tonnes, most of which is imported from the United States or Europe.

The economy ministry periodically invites local firms or agents of international companies to tender to buy wheat on behalf of the government, which usually accepts the lowest priced bid. The firms also buy wheat for the private sector. -Beirut editorial (961 1) 864148/602057
